title: The codebooks of U-559
photoNote: HMS Petard in 1943, the destroyer whose men boarded U-559. Royal Navy official photo, IWM A 21715, Crown copyright expired, public domain. The year after the boarding.
body:
Two British sailors climbed down into a sinking U-boat to steal its secrets. Neither of them came back out.

30 October 1942. Off Port Said, Egypt, the destroyer HMS Petard and other ships forced U-559 to the surface after hours of depth charge attacks. As the German crew abandoned the boat, Lieutenant Tony Fasson and Able Seaman Colin Grazier went aboard and below. Tommy Brown, a teenage canteen assistant who had lied about his age to serve, followed them.

They passed up codebooks, including the short weather cipher. Then U-559 sank, taking Fasson and Grazier with her. Brown survived.

Bletchley Park had been locked out of the U-boat code for more than ten months. With these books, it broke back in on 13 December 1942.
threads:
Two British sailors climbed down into a sinking U-boat to steal its secrets. Neither came back out.

30 October 1942, off Egypt. Tony Fasson and Colin Grazier of HMS Petard went into U-559 and passed up its codebooks. A teenage canteen assistant, Tommy Brown, carried them out. The boat sank with Fasson and Grazier aboard.

Those books helped Bletchley Park break the U-boat code again.
